note: v8 quality panel: 10 blocking findings (7 Sound Verifier, 3 Correct Reference). Coherent Contract, Protected Ground Truth and Deterministic Execution were clean. Besides the named findings, a 6,400-script random differential of the reference against GNU sed 4.9 (rev8/fuzz.py) found three reference classes the panel had not named: a b/t/T/: label ended by } or whitespace, first~0 opening a range, and a line-number range end that n/N read past (GNU closes the range without selecting that line). The reference now follows the binary on all three, 0~0 and [a-c-e] now fail as in GNU sed, and the three manual departures among them are listed in scope.md as left open (receipts ledger-receipts-v8/reference-fuzz-*.json). instruction.md is unchanged; environment/ changes only in scope.md's departure sentence.

findings.rationale: Confirmed: a 1024-byte chunking reader scored reward 1 on the returned verifier. findings.rationale: Reproduced as a contract gap rather than a reference bug: GNU sed 4.9 prints x with status 0 for -n 1,0p, and the reference does the same, while manual 4.5 says any other use of 0 gives an error and scope.md did not list the departure. Repair: scope.md now lists 'a 0 as the second address of a range' among the places where the binary departs from its manual, which are left open; no graded case uses it. The reference keeps the binary's behaviour.

gate.not_mechanizable: finding binary-vs-manual departures needs the binary; recorded as the fuzz differential in rev8/fuzz.py, which surfaced three more such places

findings.rationale: Refuted by execution: bracket() only starts a range when the character after the current one is '-', so in [-a] the leading '-' is a literal. python3 sed.py -n '/[-a]/p' on Z, -, a prints '-\na\n' with status 0, byte-identical to GNU sed 4.9; the panel's mutant (leading '-' opens a range) is already rejected by test_bracket_expressions and test_matrix_brackets on the returned snapshot. rev8 adds sweep_bracket_edges (32 cases: leading/trailing '-', leading ']', [^-a], [--/], [!--], BRE and ERE) as a further witness.

findings.rationale: Reproduced as a contract gap rather than a reference bug: with backslash as the delimiter, GNU sed 4.9 rejects an escaped embedded backslash (status 1, 'unknown command'), and so does the reference, while the manual's \%REGEXP% entry says embedded delimiters are escaped by a backslash. Under 'Scripts never fail' such a script is outside the checks, but scope.md did not say so. Repair: scope.md lists 'a backslash as the delimiter of a regular expression that itself contains a backslash' as a departure left open. Backslash as a plain delimiter is now graded (sweep_delimiters).
Confirmed (reward 1 on returned). sweep_empty_regex (10 cases) reaches // after commands skipped by a line address, by !, by b and t branches, after an address regex that did not match, and across n.
